2/3/2007, Jimi Hendrix was crowned the 'wildest guitar hero' of all-time in a poll of music fans for Classic Rock magazine. Hendrix beat Keith Richards into second place, with Stevie Ray Vaughan in third. Led Zeppelin's Jimmy Page made it to number four, followed by Dimebag Darrell, who played for several heavy metal bands including Pantera and Damageplan.
Whatshisface from The Who used to wail on it until he bled. Did he make the list?

That's why I put "music fans" in quotes. I guess Pete Townshend wasn't cute or rad enough for them. Add in the date and you can see The Who weren't touring or as popular when these kids were asked, they have no sense of history:

Townshend mimed machine gunning the crowd with his guitar while jumping on stage and playing guitar with a fast arm-windmilling motion, or stood with his arms aloft allowing his guitar to produce feedback in a posture dubbed "the Bird Man"

The reason I posted that was to exemplify that emotional and/or entertainment connection, valid components, is a different component than technical ability. Music has long been a primary form to express emotions (lately, IMO, it's mainly just a profit-driven product). Sometimes a plaintive wail speaks more than artistic accomplishment. At other times, the more talented the artist the more they enhance the message. Maybe Neil Young as opposed to Chris Squire (Yes) would be an example. Or The Ramones, who said they only knew 3 chords when they started, yet appealed to a large audience and were a pivotal point in that genre's direction. The nebulous definitions of greatest and best need to be defined for those terms to have significance, as "Art" is inherently in the eye of the beholder. With that said, at least your list has its basis clearly defined and you have the prerequisite background to voice a coherent, educated response. I'm glad you're doing this as it gives people an opportunity to assess some well-heard musicians in a more critical vein which may add to their appreciation of them. A life of dedicated practice and education deserves to be appreciated.
